newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria says its foreign reserves now top $7.0 bln.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria says its foreign reserves now top $7.0 bln.

text.p: Nigeria's external reserves have increased to more than $7.0 billion from $4.1 billion in December 1996, the national news agency said on Saturday.
The News Agency of Nigeria quoted finance minister Anthony Ani as saying the increase in reserves was a result of "public sector prudence and accountability."
Tight fiscal policies, pursued by the military government, have curtailed Nigeria's rampant inflation and stabilised the naira currency, but have also kept the economy in recession.

Nigerian economic analysts are unclear why the government is building up foreign reserves, while it leaves unpaid arrears on an external debt estimated at around $30 billion and cuts funding for crude oil production.
Some have suggested that the military government has the intention of making the naira convertible.
Recession has dogged Africa's most populous nation since political crisis erupted in 1993 after the annulment of presidential elections by a former military government.
